messages:
Nadia R: Heads-up: NovaWorks onboarding report — their staging runs spawn ~30 short-lived workers which call /v1/preflight on cold start. They hit intermittent 429s right after traffic ramp, started after they increased concurrency. Can someone help triage?

Carlos M: Thanks Nadia. Do we have client traces or headers? Are they using ephemeral tokens per worker?

Nadia R: Quick snippet from their logs:
```
2024-05-08T09:12:01Z worker-12 POST /v1/preflight 429
x-rw-ratelimit-limit: 120
x-rw-ratelimit-remaining: 0
x-rw-ratelimit-reset: 9
authorization: Bearer ephemeral ttl=20s
```
They confirmed token fetch happens inside worker init. Very likely stampede.

Carlos M: Yep, classic preflight fanout. Two-prong approach: 1) client-side fix — centralize token retrieval or cache per host, and add a small randomized jitter before first preflight; 2) server-side temporary relief — we can enable a short onboarding grace (5-10s) or raise concurrent preflight threshold for their API key while they warm up. Ops will only do this with customer request.

Sanjay D: Also check whether these are distinct IPs vs same IP. If many ephemeral IPs it looks like many clients vs one app. If same IP, they may be spawning threads and will hit our per-key concurrency guard. We should inspect the rate-limit buckets for their key.

Nadia R: They're on a serverless provider so IPs may rotate. Customer prefers app-level fixes but asked if we can provide a minimal code example and a short KB.

Carlos M: I'll draft a tiny example for Node and Python they can drop in. Node example: 
```
// node: central fetch + splay
let cachedToken = null;
async function fetchToken() {
  if (cachedToken) return cachedToken;
  // small randomized delay to avoid synchronized bursts
  await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, Math.floor(Math.random()*250)));
  cachedToken = await fetch('/internal/get-rw-token');
  return cachedToken;
}
```
Python example:
```
# python: single fetch at coldstart
_cached_token = None
async def get_token():
    global _cached_token
    if _cached_token:
        return _cached_token
    await asyncio.sleep(random.random()*0.25)
    _cached_token = await fetch_token_from_backend()
    return _cached_token
```

Sanjay D: Also recommend honoring x-rw-ratelimit-reset header and implementing exponential backoff + jitter. Suggested policy: initial wait = min(1s, reset), then backoff factor 2, jitter +/-25%, cap 30s. Document that in KB.

ops-bot: ops: request received to temporarily raise preflight concurrency for api-key rd_abc123 for 10 minutes. Must be approved by oncall.

Carlos M: I'll coordinate with Ops oncall — we can offer a one-time 10m warmup window if they need immediate relief while they patch. But prefer customer implements token caching.

Nadia R: I'll send the code snippets + recommended backoff to NovaWorks and ask them to test with a gradual ramp (5% increments over 15 minutes). I'll also include instructions to watch x-rw-ratelimit-remaining.

Sanjay D: I'll create the KB draft and add a short troubleshooting checklist: check token churn, check token TTL, verify if preflight originates from many IPs, implement splay, implement cache, and honor reset header. Tagging @Carlos for review.

Nadia R: Thanks team. Will circle back after they test. If they still see issues, I'll request ops warmup and add details here. :thumbsup:
